abstract: We study no-three-in-line selections from dyadic square-grid sources having at most two points in every column and every modular fibre $ax+y=c$. The exact full sources are binary-isometry designs with ordinary no-three capacity at most $3N/2$. We extend this obstruction to sources with growing deficits. A weighted rounding lemma on the binary prefix tree gives a full design containing all but at most $11d$ existing points of any source of size $2N-d$. Consequently, every sublinear-deficit sequence has ordinary capacity at most $3N/2+o(N)$, and the entire strengthened modular class has capacity at most $47N/24$. The rounding lemma requires only the column cap and yields a separate necessary condition for arbitrary ordinary caps: a cap of size $m>7N/4$ has weighted same-parity modular collision energy at least $(4m-7N)^2/32$. Thus a cap above $1.8N$ requires energy greater than $N^2/800$. For full binary affine sources, that energy is either zero or at least $N^2/2$, demonstrating a limitation of the criterion. The proofs combine pair saturation, disjoint tree charges, and an exhaustive size-eight isometry certificate. Standalone finite controls and an independent analytic and computational audit support the results. These are structural restrictions: they provide neither an unbounded construction above $1.8N$ nor an impossibility theorem for the unrestricted problem.

title: Stable completion of dyadic modular caps and a necessary collision energy
